limitations: The confidence model uses conditional-independent binary flags with shared sensitivity and false-positive rates, not calibrated production confidence scores.
The analysis inherits E62-E64's finite binary state matrix, pacing-window grid, and fitted-service simulation.
True states are equally weighted; a production traffic distribution can change expected throughput and violation probability.
Safety is deterministic only when every mistaken keyed feature is flagged; missed low-confidence errors retain residual risk.
The lookup has no temporal hysteresis, switching cost, reject/defer action, or online confidence calibration.
model: Condition an uncertainty-safe pacing lookup on per-feature confidence flags. A flagged feature may take either binary value; an unflagged feature is fixed to its estimate. The selected window must be SLO-feasible for every keyed state in that confidence set.

strategy.confidence_set_safe: Use confidence flags to form an axis-aligned set of possible true keys, then select the maximum-throughput window that is robustly SLO-feasible for every state in the set.
strategy.hamming1_safe_baseline: E64 static envelope covering every key within Hamming distance one, regardless of which feature is low confidence.
strategy.naive_baseline: E64 estimated-key lookup with no safety set.

validation.safety_probability_ordering: For every record, scenario violation probability is no greater than unsafe-path probability, which is no greater than confidence-miss probability.
